utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is sitting with two Judges, and we'll continue the proceedings under Rule 15 bis, subparagraph A, because Judge Lindholm is not able to be with us due to illness. The Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please. It's necessary for us now to go into -- I believe the term is private session. That is the suppression of sound. It doesn't have to be a fully closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: But the content of what is said needs to be suppressed, so I'd ask that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please sit down. Yes. The blinds can be lifted. Yes, the Prosecution can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you state your name for the record. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I have no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you state your name, please.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: 8th of March, 1957.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So that makes you 45 years old?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Two sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where were you born, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where was your father born?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And your mother?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long had your father's family lived in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Since mid-nineteenth century.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Of what ethnic group do you belong?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Of which political parties have you been a member?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia, then I was a member of the Croatian Democratic Union, and also a member of the SDA party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you were a member of the Communist Party, did you hold any position?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what position did you hold?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I was a delegate in the Municipal Assembly, as a member of the League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And at this time, do you belong to any political parties?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to go over your educational background. Where did you go to school?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I completed my elementary education in Bosanski Samac, the high school for electrical engineering I completed in Odzak. In 1976 I enrolled on a course of electrical engineering in Sarajevo, where I spent a year. After that I got married, got a job, and then I continued my studies at the same time as I worked, in Subotica and in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And while you were working in Subotica and Novi Sad, what were you studying?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I studied in a two-year electrical engineering college, and then in Novi Sad I went to the two-year course for expert associate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you hold an engineering degree at this time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, I do not have an engineering degree, but I do have a degree that one gets after this two-year course. In our system it was the sixth degree of education, the sixth level of education.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it would probably be called an associate's degree in electrical engineering in many of the Western states; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you ever in the military in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did my national service.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When did you do your national service?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I served it in 1978 and 1979, in the centre for reserve officers in Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever attend reserve officer's school?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said. I attended the reserve officer's school in Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Now, upon completion, did you attain a certain rank?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After I completed my duty at the JNA, I attained the rank of second lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after 1979, did you receive any additional training?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Up until 1986 I did several types of training in the Engineering Corps of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you attain another rank other than second lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After that I attained the rank of lieutenant, then the rank of captain. In 1986 I became the commander of the Engineering Corps in, in a corps that belonged to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you a professional soldier, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not a professional soldier. I was a reserve officer in the professional military.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as a reserve officer, how many months did you spend in the military each year?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately two months every year.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, not being a professional soldier, I believe you had to work. Where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I worked for Elektrodistribucija in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what was that? What type of business was that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: This was a state-owned company that distributed electricity. So its basic job was distribution and the continuous supply of electricity to consumers, the end users.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In what area did you provide the electricity? Was this just in the town of Bosanski Samac or outside that area?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: We supplied neighbouring municipalities also with the electrical -- with electricity: Orasje, Odzak, Modrica, and of course all the local communes in our municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When did you start working there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I worked there twice. The first time, before my -- going away to college and before I completed my military service, and then after the military, from 1979 until the end of 1991, until December of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you started working there, let's say on a full-time basis, in 1979, what position did you hold?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I did more than one thing. The majority of my time there I spent first as a manager of the department for measuring and protecting the electrical devices, and then for some six years I worked as the manager of the technical division.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as manager of the technical division, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: As part of my job description, I was responsible mostly for the continuous supply of electricity, for the quality of that electricity that was being distributed, so for the continuity of supply, removal of problems, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you supervise a number of people in this position, as head of the technical unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: In this job, I had about six work groups. All together there were about 52 people in these groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, having spent most of your life in Bosanski Samac, I'm going to ask you if you know some people. Are you familiar with a man by the name of Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long have you known Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I have known him for about 25 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Having known him for that long period of time, I'd ask you to look around this courtroom, and could you tell me if he's sitting in this courtroom at this time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is. He is in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you please point him out and describe him.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: He is the man who is sitting on the third from the left, and he's wearing glasses. On the left side from where I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long have you known Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I have known him for about 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I'd ask you to look around this courtroom and tell us if he's seated in this courtroom at this time.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is sitting in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us where he's sitting?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The second from the left. He's also wearing glasses. He's grey-haired.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you know a man by the name of Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I have known him for about 20 years, maybe a little bit longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is he sitting in this courtroom at this time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you please point him out too to the Court.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: He's the first from the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that all three defendants have been identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just one more question. Are you familiar with a man by the name of Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I've known him for about 20 years, maybe a little bit longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go back to the late spring and early summer of 1991. Could you tell the Court during that time period what the atmosphere was like in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the atmosphere in Bosanski Samac resembled a normal atmosphere, although the citizens of Bosanski Samac felt a certain fear because war was in their neighbourhood, in Croatia, and they were afraid that this war could spill over to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, are you familiar with a cafe known as the Cafe Molla?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with the name of that cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where is that located?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: It's very close to the city market.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, in the late spring and early summer of 1991, did you happen to visit the Cafe Molla?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you went there during that time period, did you receive any information or were you made aware of any rumours at that time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: At that time that we're talking about, a polarisation in the town could already be felt amongst members of different ethnic groups. So there were cafes or restaurants where only Muslims or only Croats would go; only Serbs would go to other cafes. There were some cafes that everybody frequented. I would very often go to the cafe called Molla, and townsfolk that were Muslim would mostly gather there. Sometimes a Croat would also show up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, during that time that you were going to the Cafe Molla, did you hear any rumours, let's say, relating to weapons? Did you hear any rumours relating to weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was a very visited place. I said that this cafe was close to the city market, and in this cafe I heard that some trucks with weapons were coming to Bosanski Samac and that certain people in Bosanski Samac were arming themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: People of what ethnic group did you hear were arming themselves in the late spring and early summer of 1991 in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: They were of the Serb ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how often did you hear these rumours in the late spring and summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I'd hear them several times. Once somebody from the town came, and this person said that a truck had arrived with weapons, and it came to the area of town that was called Novo Naselje, or the New Settlement, Sokolusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when someone came to the cafe Molla and told you that, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were rumours all over the place, and some of them were true and some of them weren't. I got in my car and drove towards Novo Naselje because I wanted to check this piece of information, and indeed I saw a truck with weapons. There were some cases on this truck, actually. I assume weapons were in the cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's take it one step at a time. What hour of the day or night were you told that there was a truck of weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: This was after 9.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you went to the area known as the New Settlement and you saw a truck. Could you describe it, as best you can recall?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: This was a truck, capacity about seven tonnes. Well, it's hard to explain. I think that was the standard type of truck. And there were some wooden cases in it, and some young men were unloading these weapons in front of a house which belongs to a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, it had these wooden cases. Could you describe them, as best you can.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Wooden cases. It was long, say about a metre, metre and a half. The height was maybe 30 centimetres and the width about 80 centimetres, something like that, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And these boxes which were being unloaded off a truck sometime after 9.00 at night, had you ever seen boxes like that before or since?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I had seen them before, and of course I saw them later as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what were found, or what were those boxes used to hold?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Usually they used to hold semi-automatic and automatic rifles, also M-48 rifles, and also equipment for maintaining of those rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: These people that were removing these boxes, did you ever see them at some later time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw them later. They were members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, as the summer continued in 1991, did you hear any other rumours about weapons being distributed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The same thing happened in the town, in the settlement that was built behind the stadium. Also a fellow townsperson came. He was a Muslim. And he told us that weapons had also arrived in that part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, when did this happen, this incident occur, that someone told you that weapons were being -- that a truck with weapons had arrived in the area by the stadium? During what month in the summer, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: This was maybe at the beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did they say that it was being delivered or it was being unloaded near a certain house?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This truck was unloaded close to the house of Stevo, nicknamed Para.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what did you do after hearing this information? Did you do anything to confirm it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I sent a young man to there. He went there on his bike. He went towards the house of Stevo, Para, and he came back quite quickly. And he said that he saw the truck and he saw that people were unloading something off the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did he describe the boxes that were being unloaded, when he said something was being unloaded off the truck? Did he say it was boxes?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said that they were rifles. He was also in the military, so he must have known. He must have known that they were rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What time of day or night did this occur?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: This also happened in the evening, around 9.30/10.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you receive any other information during the summer of 1991 concerning people receiving arms in the villages surrounding Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Tell the Court what information you had received during the summer of 1991.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: In the summer of that year, 1991, I found out that in all the villages -- in all the Serb villages in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, weapons had been handed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, I wonder whether you could clarify with the witness these boxes that both he and the person on the bicycle saw being taken off the trucks. Apart from the dimensions of the boxes, was it noticeable that there was any lettering, any symbols, any marks that would identify these as belonging to the military and so on? Apart from they were wooden boxes and they were of a certain size, was there anything else on those boxes?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, you heard the Judge's question. Was there any notations or anything about those boxes which indicated to you that they contained weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: These were standard cases into which weapons of the kind that I mentioned were put. They were standard-issue cases. They were made specifically for the transportation of weapons of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Having served in the army for, at that point for 12 years, had you ever seen those kind of standard cases at any of the military bases which you served on?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. I had an opportunity to see them, carry them, and all other kinds of things. It was indisputably like those other cases. They were the real cases, the original cases. There's no doubt about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, that time when you saw them, I know it was dark and these were being unloaded in the night-time, but were you able to see any markings or were you able to determine from the licence plates on the trucks where either the boxes came from or where those trucks came from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Since the weapons were being unloaded off the end of the truck, when you open the back of the truck, the licence plates get covered, so I couldn't see them. I couldn't see what the licence plates were. On the cases themselves, I didn't see any letters, but I know that those were cases for housing semi-automatic and automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you or any of your friends or colleagues speak to any persons in the town or in those surrounding villages who indicated that they were receiving weapons at that time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what did they tell you, your friends, or your colleagues about receiving weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Since there were also members of my ethnicity that belonged to these units, and I didn't know that the unit was called the 4th Detachment at the time, some of them informed me regularly about the events when the weapons would arrive, who would get the weapons, who the members of this unit were, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, were you able to learn whether any of the political parties were involved in the distribution of weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And which political parties did you learn were involved in distributing these weapons, or automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I heard about it and I was convinced of it myself. This party was called the Movement for Yugoslavia. And at the later stages, the SDP also did that, that is to say, the party -- I think the Social Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, in which villages were these automatic weapons being distributed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, the weapons were distributed in Serbian villages. I can name some of them: Obudovac, Crkvina, Batkusa, Pisari, Skaric, Kruskovo Polje, Brvnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were these distributed randomly or were these distributed on a large scale, sir, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: The weapons were distributed to the people who were on the reserve force of the then Territorial Defence, to the residents in the Serb local communes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's 3.45. Would you like to take the break now or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll take the break now and continue our proceedings at 1615 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution is continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Good afternoon, Mr. Fitozovic. Now, when we left off, we were talking about the distribution of arms in the Serb villages surrounding Bosanski Samac. And was this done on a random basis or was this being done on a large-scale basis? Were a lot of people receiving guns or was it just a limit -- a person here, a person there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: In the Serb villages in the vicinity, in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, this was done publicly and en masse. In the town itself, it was done more discreetly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you continue to hear these rumours over a several-month period, of weapons being distributed to Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did continue to hear such rumours, and I also continued to listen and to observe. On several occasions I visited the area, I mean the Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what were you able to learn?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: On one occasion during my working hours I went to the local commune of Obudovac, and at the local cooperative I noticed a large number of people wearing the uniforms of the former JNA. Then, in the area of Barice - that was a farm in Obudovac - I saw a certain number of guns, cannons, Howitzers, mortars, tanks. And then when I visited the other part of the municipality, in the Kruskovo Polje local commune, there were also tanks located there. Then in the local commune of Skaric, which is close to close to Bosanski Samac itself, there were mortars there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's take this a step at a time. Obudovac, where you saw some of these large guns and you saw some -- or you saw tanks and large guns and you saw some JNA troops, what is the ethnic composition of that town?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: 100 per cent Serb population lived in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What about in the other area that you saw these mortars, in Skaric?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: It was also a Serb village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How many mortars do you recall seeing in the village of Skaric?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I think around six.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were these pointing in a particular direction?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were pointing in the direction of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how far was Bosanski Samac from the village of Skaric?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: As the crow flies, around 4 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is 4 kilometres within mortar range?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, troops being stationed in Obudovac, JNA troops, is that usual? Was that something that was common?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: That was not usual, in view of the fact that there wasn't a barracks in Obudovac or in any other local commune in the territory of the Bosanski Samac municipality, nor were there any permanent military installations where the troops would be housed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What about having large guns, tanks, mortars in the villages surrounding Bosanski Samac? Was that normal? Was that common or usual?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, that was not usual. This kind of equipment, I mean tanks and Howitzers, that was something that belonged to the units of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Had you ever had that type of equipment in that area, in the former TO, or stationed in that area, previously?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No. The TO never had any tanks, Howitzers, and other weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What were you thinking when you saw the troops and all this weaponry, this heavy weaponry, in the area surrounding Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What were you thinking or how did you feel when you saw all of this weaponry, this heavy weaponry, tanks and mortars, in the areas surrounding Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, naturally, I didn't feel comfortable, and nor did the other residents in Bosanski Samac municipality, Muslims and Croats alike. It looked like something that had been seen before in the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was that prior to the war there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. Could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said that it looked like something that you had seen before in the Republic of Croatia. Are you talking about the build-up of arms in the Republic of Croatia prior to the war occurring in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's continue a little bit back, speaking of Croatia. Had you been to Croatia at the end of the summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I spent my vacation in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where were you in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Tuheljske Toplice spa.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And at some point did you return home to Bosnia from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After my vacation, I headed back to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in what mode of transportation did you return to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I returned on a bus. That was the Zagreb-Tuzla line.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And approximately on what date did you return to Croatia - I'm sorry - did you return to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: It may have been around the 22nd of August, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did something happen to you on that trip back to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, something unpleasant happened. In the town of Okucani, or Novi Varos -- Okucani.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where is Okucani related -- I'm sorry, located? Where is Okucani located? Is it in Croatia or is it in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Okucani is in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And tell the Court what happened -- please tell the Court what happened in Okucani?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: On the way back to Bosnia, on the motor way in Okucani, we were stopped by the reservists of the Yugoslav People's Army, and some other soldiers who were probably doing their national service in the JNA, and also they were the professional soldiers. They stopped the bus and made us get off the bus, all of us. There may have been about 40 or 45 of us on the bus. All were men. They checked our ID cards and they established that the majority of the persons aboard the bus were Muslims. In fact, the bus that I took was the bus used by the people originally from Bosnia who worked in Croatia. They used this service to go home, and by coincidence, I also took this bus. And by coincidence, most of the people on the bus were Muslims. I wore jeans and a white shirt, which was transparent. It had a breast pocket on the left side. Since I smoked at the time, I had a pack of cigarettes in this pocket, and the brand of cigarettes was Croatia. A reservist approached me, tore the pocket off, and hit me here in the neck with his fist. And I had a haemotoma there as a result, and also there was some bleeding, so the collar of the shirt was slightly stained with blood. After a certain period of time, we managed to reach Slavonski Brod, using some auxiliary roads. I got off the bus in Slavonski Brod and called my friend from a phone booth, a friend in Bosanski Samac. His name was Muris Focakovic, nicknamed Murat, and he picked me up in Slavonski Brod.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just to clarify this a little bit. When you were stopped, had the Serb military taken over that town in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I think that maybe on that day that the Serb military did take that town. I don't know whether it was on that day or the day after. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you also said that there were JNA soldiers, reservists and regulars. Were there any soldiers from Serbia that you noticed by way of their dress?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Since until that time I had lots of dealings with the army, I mean the legitimate army, I saw the difference between the soldiers who belonged to the regular units of the JNA, and I was able to distinguish the persons belonging to the reserve force. They did not have the type of clothes that the JNA soldiers at that time wore. They wore beards. Some of them used the Ekavian dialect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder, Mr. Weiner, whether you could find out from the witness whether he went on holiday to Croatia on his own, was he married at the time, with the two children at the time? Did they remain in Bosanski Samac? Did they go to Croatia on holiday, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You heard the Judge's question. Did you go to Croatia on your own or were you with your family?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I took the vacation on my own. My family was at the seaside at the time, and I went to the spa.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Just one supplemental question, just to confirm what you said, because I can't find it in the transcript. The bus that you were returning on from Croatia to Bosnia, all the passengers were male and there were no children; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were no children. All the passengers were male. I know that for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And these men with the long beards who spoke the Ekavian accent, they let you go eventually?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: They let us go. They searched the luggage, searching for things of interest to them. The luggage contained my personal belongings, and so did the luggage of other passengers. So they let us go, but we took the side roads. We did not continue on on the motorway.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the long beards and speaking with an Ekavian accent, did they also have those cockade hats, those black cockade hats?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They also had this type of gear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's consistent with them being from Serbia, is it not, between the dress and the accent?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It looked like they were from Serbia. In fact, I'm quite familiar with the way they speak, because my mother was born in Serbia and I went to my mother's birthplace quite often, and they spoke in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, that was August of 1991. Let's move to the fall. During the fall or autumn of 1991, basically September, October, and even into November, were you hearing any other rumours relating to reservists in Bosanski Samac? Did you hear any rumours about reservists?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: The situation in early September began to be more complex as regards the interethnic tolerance and also some unknown persons were spotted in the town. They wore civilian clothes, but we didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But did you hear any rumours about reservists being sent to certain places, reservists from Bosanski Samac and the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that after my vacation I started working again, I remember very well that on the 1st or 2nd of September, I heard at work that some people of Serb ethnic background were going to Serbia to get additional training or some kind of specialist training.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where were they being sent after they received specialist training in Serbia, these people from Bosanski Samac, after they were sent to Serbia for special training, where were they then sent?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: After completing specialist training in Serbia, then the next contingent would go to receive the training, and the individuals who completed the course, or the specialist course, would go to the front line in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where were the front lines in Croatia at that time that they were sending the people from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: The nearest front line was in Vukovar, and that's where they went. They went to fight in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, these rumours that you heard about Serbs from Bosanski Samac being sent to Serbia for training and then being sent to Vukovar in Croatia to fight, were you able to confirm any of this in September or October of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you ever able to confirm these rumours that people from Bosanski Samac were being sent to Serbia for training and then being sent to Croatia to fight, to Vukovar, Croatia, to fight? Were you ever able to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was able to confirm that during my usual activities at work. Some people from my company went to have this specialist training and then to the Vukovar theatre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell the Court, or can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, before you proceed, if you look at line 18, that's page 41, when you asked the question about him hearing rumours about Serbs from Bosanski Samac being sent to Serbia for training, you mentioned September/October 1992. Is that the correct year?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I -- when I spoke -- when I asked you a question, I said in September/October of 1992. We're speaking of September or October of 1991; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that some men, young men from your company, and that's the electrical distribution plant, or the electrical power plant, were sent for training and then sent to Vukovar. Could you tell us their names, if you can recall them, those young men that were sent?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Savo Bajic was absent from work for a certain period of time. He is from Crkvina. Then Bosko Marinkovic and Stojan Milicevic. They were -- they did not go at the same time. One of them would go and then when he returned, another one would go. And they were absent from the company for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you said they were absent, are we talking about a few days or are we talking about months?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Several months. Some of them I didn't see from September of that year up until today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you able to learn where they were?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I found out where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you found out that they were out there fighting in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let us move along in the fall of 1991. Did you know a man by the name of Sulejman Tihic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how long had you known Sulejman Tihic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: For about 30 years, maybe even longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in 1991, did he hold any position in any party in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What position did he hold? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: He was the president of the Party of Democratic Action of the municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sometime early in that month, did you happen to meet or see Sulejman Tihic early in the month of September 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you have some conversation concerning the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We talked daily about political events of the day, about the safety situation in the town, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sometime while you were talking, did he approach you about joining the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He asked me to join the party of the SDA, the Party of the Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did he offer you a position in the party if you were to join?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that as the president of the party, he had the right - and this was part of his presidential duties - he had the right to make me a member of the city council of the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you agree to join?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agreed, and I joined the SDA. Immediately after that, I also became a member of the city council of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that was in September of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, also in that month, were you given any other appointment by the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what appointment were you given in addition to the town board or city council?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: When I became a town board member, I was named to become a member of the Executive Council of the SDA for Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that appointment to the Executive Council, was that also in September?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All this happened very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you receive any other appointments from the SDA party in September of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Tell the Court what other appointment you received?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Within this Executive Council of the SDA, there were certain commissions, and I was made the president of the security safety commission of the SDA, and this was on the municipality level.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you appointed by Sulejman Tihic to that, or were you appointed by the town council or the Executive Council to that position, the executive board?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: The executive board of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How many people were on this commission on security and safety?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: There were three men in this commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you hold a particular role on that commission?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What position?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I was the president of this commission for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did the commission for security and safety do? What was their role?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Its role was predominantly to estimate the situation in the town, in the municipality, and generally in that part of Bosnian Posavina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who else was on that committee, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. This was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after you were to analyse or review the security situation in the town and surrounding areas of the Posavina, were you to report to anyone your findings?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And who were you to report to your findings?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: My findings I first reported to the Executive Council, that is to say, the president of the Executive Council, and that office was held by Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, let's continue in September 1991. Did you make a decision in relation to establishing a military unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You decided to establish your own military unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, not a personal military unit. On the executive board, I told Sulejman Tihic, the president of SDA, that the situation in the town, in municipality, and in the region was very complex, that there was a lot of weapons surrounding us, that Serbs were armed, and it was clear that none of us Muslims were armed. And at that time I told Tihic -- I told him the following: If he wanted me, I would still be the president of the safety commission, but I wanted him to get some arms so that we could also have some weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to that conversation with Mr. Tihic, you wanted weapons for what? Were you putting together a military unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My intention was to create a unit whose purpose would be to defend the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, had any local citizens from Bosanski Samac or the surrounding area approached you about putting together a military unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, when you told Sulejman Tihic that you needed weapons, how did he respond, when you asked him if he could get you some weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: He got scared from my idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you have a similar conversation with Izet Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: He was there when I suggested this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were they both scared when you asked them about supplying weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were both scared. But it's true that Izetbegovic wasn't as worried.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So he seemed less worried than Sulejman Tihic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was less worried than Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, this unit that you were putting together to protect the town, was this going to be a unit of the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was this going to be a unit of the HDZ party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was it going to be a unit tied to any political party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was it a unit tied to an ethnic organisation or an ethnic group? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who was going to be invited into this, if you want to call it, independent military unit to protect the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: All the citizens of Bosanski Samac. That means Serbs, Croats, and Muslims alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was this unit going to be similar to or different from the unit that was later developed called the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: It was supposed to be different from this unit which had already existed in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why was the independent unit that you were developing going to be different from that of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, this unit would have preserved the town the way it was, that is to say, it would have remained a multi-ethnic town and part of the state of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What, in your view, was the goal of the 4th Detachment, then?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: The goal of the 4th Detachment was to turn this area of Bosanski Samac into a Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, and it was supposed to become a part of some Republika Srpska, which now exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what's the basis of your opinion that the 4th Detachment was trying to turn Bosanski Samac into a Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: You mean it was supposed to be turned into a Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. You indicated that your unit was an independent military unit to protect the town of Bosanski Samac and keep it the way it was. However, the 4th Detachment, you indicated, was different in that it was supposed to -- that it was trying to turn Bosanski Samac into a Republika Srpska, as it now exists. Why did you believe the 4th Detachment wanted to change Bosanski Samac and turn it into a Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: For the following reason: As I said, the surrounding Serb villages were armed, all of them, all of the Serb villages. The town itself was also armed. All the Serbs in the town were armed, and also the 4th Detachment was armed by the JNA. There was also some kind of a Territorial Defence that had nothing at all. There were only two men there, two figureheads, but all the warehouses were empty. The JNA had previously emptied those warehouses and distributed the arms to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. You indicated that Mr. Tihic and Mr. Izetbegovic were nervous and worried about arming the unit. Were you afraid of arming this unit that you were establishing, this independent unit to protect Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I was not afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I can say freely that it was for the following reason: I was a soldier. I had certain amount of military knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you go ahead and establish a unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How many men were in this unit in the beginning?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: There were about 80 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And eventually, by December of 1991, how many men were in this unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, somewhere around 80 men. At the very beginning there were about 80, and then in December there were about 200 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were all of these men of the Muslim ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were these all members of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were there people of other ethnic groups in this unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were people of other ethnic groups there as well. There were Croats, there were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last portion of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you repeat what you said after "Albanians"?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: There were also Gypsies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were there any persons from mixed marriages in the unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was even one member who was from a Serbo-Croat marriage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you have enough weapons to give to all of these members of this incident army in the beginning, in September/October?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have enough weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you started this unit, did everyone -- sorry. When you started this unit, did you have any weapons to give out?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Not in the first stage. Later I had about -- well, actually, not about; exactly 20 automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that. But in the beginning, was every member given a rifle or a gun or a weapon of some kind upon joining?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, sometime later - we won't get into specifics yet - but sometime later, were you able to acquire or procure weapons for this unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, later I managed to procure 20 automatic rifles. They were originally manufactured in the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go to October of 1991. Do you recall procuring 30 Genschers?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What is a Genscher?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: This is a type of automatic rifle made in Germany, and that's probably why it's called what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were these older automatic weapons? Were these the ones that were made during world war two?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These were older weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were these purchased from a government agency?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, they weren't bought.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How did you acquire them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Privately, through private channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were these purchased by the SDA or any other political party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No. The SDA didn't buy them. The president himself was scared of that, as I said, at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And once you got these 30 older automatic weapons, what did you do with them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I distributed these weapons to those members that I considered braver.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Weiner. I wonder whether the witness could tell us if these Genschers were purchased privately, through private channels, and the SDA didn't buy them, who provided the financing to buy these weapons which were purchased privately and not from a government agency? So where did the money come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The question from Judge Williams was: If the SDA didn't buy them, who provided the financing for the purchase -- for the private purchase of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't talking about any finances. I just said that I procured these weapons privately. I might have stolen them, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, shouldn't that be cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm working on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I mean, if he did steal them, then he better say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- or let's take a step back. Were you involved in the finances with relation to these firearms or guns?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know any of the details of the financing -- of the finances of the procurement of these guns?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know how these guns were procured?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how it was procured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, we can't have that type of answer when he had just said that he procured these weapons privately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let me -- I'm going to get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you personally procure these weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the Court would like to know how you procured them.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Izet Izetbegovic helped me with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did he handle the financial end, if there was one?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I didn't get involved with the finances. All I asked for was the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Izet Izetbegovic somehow obtained them or procured them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He procured it and I took it from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you have any idea how or where he obtained them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Any further questions from the panel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you able to procure weapons in November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court how you procured weapons in November of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In November 1991, a truck with Slovenian licence plates, or Ljubljana licence plates - I know that the name of the company was Viator. That's what it said on the canvas top - transported weapons across the bridge on the River Sava, and the vehicle broke down in the area between the railway station and the bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: After it broke down, did someone notify you that this truck had broken down?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They found me in the town and they informed me about the situation, about the fact that a truck had broken down in the area between the railway station and the bus station in Bosanski Samac and that the driver had insisted that the truck be towed away in order to be repaired or that some other action be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you go out and meet with the driver?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went there to see what was going on, and then I learned that the truck had weapons for Sarajevo or for Central Bosnia and that assistance was needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you render that assistance?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I helped them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Tell us what you did.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: I told the young man to find Smail Smailovic, who was a truck driver employed in the veterinary station in Bosanski Samac. The truck owned by the veterinary station in Bosanski Samac was the same size as the truck that had broken down. They found Smail Smailovic - I think his last name is Smailovic- he did as I told him and took the truck from the veterinary station, and we towed the truck, I mean the truck with the Slovenian licence plates, and we offloaded the weapons and loaded them onto the truck that belonged to the veterinary station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As a result of helping them by towing the truck, unloading the weapons, loading them -- getting them in other vehicle, where you loaded the weapons into another vehicle, did they give you any sort of reward?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That was the deal that was struck immediately. We took two crates with the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how many weapons were in the two crates?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: There were 20 automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did this Smail Smailovic drive these to some place in Bosnia, not the 20, but the remaining weapons, for those people from Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It drove to its final destination. I don't know what it was, nor was I interested in finding that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as an aside, this Smail Smailovic, was he the gentleman who, some month later, drove Tota Ramusovic to the hospital after he was shot?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Tota.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. No. That's not the Smajl.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, these two boxes of automatic rifles that you got --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Weiner. I'm not sure whether the last answer makes sense when you were asked about Tota being driven to the hospital and the answer is: "No, no, no. That's not the Smajl." Maybe you can clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Some months later, in February or March - and we're going to be talking about it later - there was a shoot-out where Danilo and Tota Ramusovic were shot, and someone drove them to the doctor or the hospital. Was that another Smajl or was that this Smajl, Smail Smailovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: That was not Smail Smailovic. That was another man --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: -- who drove Tota and the rest to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, with regard to this transfer of weapons, you were notified that this truck had become disabled and your help was needed to tow the truck away and transfer the weapons and get another truck to carry the weapons off. Did Sulejman Tihic, Izet Izetbegovic, or any member of the SDA notify you that this truck was disabled?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was not informed by Sulejman Tihic or by Izet Izetbegovic. I was notified by a member of our unit. He told me that the truck had broken down and he found me in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that the SDA and HDZ and the political parties had nothing to do with this incident relating to the transfer of weapons and assisting the disabled truck?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I don't regard this to be an incident, and I also say that the SDA and the HDZ did not have anything to do with the weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have an objection to the manner in which my learned colleague is conducting the examination, because -- and this is not the first time he's asking leading questions. Perhaps he could ask who notified him about the incident with the truck and not to lead the witness in this way, by supplying the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: A leading question is one that supplies the exact answer, which the witness will then respond to. If I ask him whether or not Izet Izetbegovic or Sulejman Tihic had anything to do with this, it could be yes, it could be no, it could be possibly, it could be both of them. I've got to lead them to somebody as having --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, meaning that the question itself would be suggestive of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. If I said -- if knowing that, let's say, Mr. X was involved, and I said: Wasn't Mr. X involved? And his only answer is yes, Mr. X was involved. That's leading. This is -- I'm asking about a specific area. It's not -- slightly leading, but it's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not strictly a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's move on, sir, to December of 1991. As of that time, how many weapons had you procured?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Fifty pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, had -- on each procurement -- let's start off with October- were you given ammunition with these guns?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Not on each. Let's take the one in October. When you got the 30 German rifles, automatic rifles, from World War II. Were you given any ammunition at that time to go with those rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did receive a small quantity, about 15 bullets per each rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next procurement. In November, when you received a gift of 20 rifles, were you given any ammunition at that time with those 20 automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't get any ammunition, because the truck did not carry any ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to object to the formulation of the question on page 57, line 18. The Prosecutor said that -- talked about a gift, and the witness himself said that it was the result of a deal on the -- involving the repair of the truck. So I would like to have the question rephrased.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll use the word "receipt" of the weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. I think I can see what the counsel is protesting about. You are suggesting that it was a gift. Yes. Can you rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In November, when you received these 20 automatic rifles, did you receive -- I'm just asking you this again for the record - did you receive any ammunition with those 20 rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not receive any ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you've started this military unit to protect the town of Bosanski Samac. What were the functions, other than protecting Bosanski Samac? What type of functions was this unit performing in September/October - basically September through the end of the year? What type of functions was the unit performing?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: During the night, the unit manned two checkpoints. During the day, it observed the town. So that in this manner we gathered information about the movements of the JNA units, of the reservists, and finally, members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's start with the daytime. Did you have patrols during the daytime?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We patrolled the town in daytime in order to see whether there have been any changes in the town, whether any people from the outside had come in, whether there were any armed people, any people in uniform there, whether any troops were passing through the town or around the town. By that I mean the JNA or the reservists. And so on. Simply, we observed the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why were you making these observations? Had there been some change in the area in the last several months?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All kinds of things were happening in the town. There were people from abroad, who were not from the municipality of Bosanski Samac. Some people in uniforms were passing through. There were also some cases of verbal insults being traded, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, how many patrols did you have in the daytime?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: We patrolled throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how many patrols did you have? Was it one patrol, two, three, four, five?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Two or three patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how many people were in each one of these patrolling groups?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: There would be two men in each.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you just patrol the town of Bosanski Samac or did you -- were the villagers also patrolled?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes in the villages too, but mostly in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what did they do with this information concerning people that they had seen and anything that they had noted? What would they do with this information?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: The information was relayed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: These patrols, these two or three men -- these two or three -- two-man patrols, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were any of the daytime patrols armed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, never. No daytime patrol ever had arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were these walking patrols or were these people in vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: The patrols in the town were on foot. Like all the other civilians, they were virtually indistinguishable from other civilians, other citizens. We called them the patrols.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the witness a question. So these daytime patrols, were they under a commander? If they were in groups of two or three or four, was one of them in charge of each little patrol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No one was in command of the others. There would be just two men. They would go there together and they had the same task. Nobody was in charge of anybody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And I just have one other question. You state, page 60, line 7, that they were virtually indistinguishable from other civilians." My question is: Virtually indistinguishable? Were they in some way distinguishable, by perhaps wearing a special item of clothing or having a badge or insignia of some type? So I would like to know: Were they in some way distinguishable by what they were wearing or some insignia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were not distinguishable in any way. They wore civilian clothes, just like all the other citizens who happened to be in the town in any given location, in a cafe, in the street, in a shop, and so on. They could not be distinguished from the rest of the population. They could only be distinguished from the soldiers, because they did not wear any uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did these daytime patrols ever set up any checkpoints or barricades?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they ever stop vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What about pedestrians? Did they ever stop pedestrians?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No pedestrian was ever stopped or had his or her ID checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you or the police ever receive a complaint about any of these people?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, we never received any complaints.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were these people ever involved in an incident of violence or crime of any kind?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: No, never. They were not criminals. These were just ordinary citizens who had this duty to patrol the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did the general public even know that they were out there patrolling and watching events in the town?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: The public knew about the night-time patrols, but they didn't know about the daytime patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the night-time patrols. What type of patrols and units did you have out there in the night-time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: In the night-time we had two patrols stationed at the entrance to the town: one on the east entrance, and the other was stationed on the south entrance to the town, from the direction of Crkvina and Tisina and Slavonski Samac, or from the direction of the railway station. It was set up at an intersection, or, to be more specific, it was stationed by the Muslim and Catholic cemeteries.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, were these patrols that were stationed in those two areas, were these people on foot or were they in vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Those patrols were in passenger cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How many people would be in a passenger car?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: On a night-time patrol there would be three men in a passenger car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what would they be doing?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Their task was to control, to observe visually the persons entering or exiting the town, any movements of the troops that I mentioned earlier, any activities on the part of the 4th Detachment, and so on. They were stationary, and one was stationed next to the hospital, and the other, as I have already said, next to the Muslim and Catholic cemeteries.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were these people armed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The night-time patrols were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they stop vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC
